correctness.rationale: The universal-algebra term-function realization is exact because the base algebra is finite. Every iterated bracket has coefficient J_s times an elementary scalar syzygy multiplied by a polynomial in the commuting operators a_i J_s; there are no bracket terms between derived functions. At any nonzero a, these polynomial values fill B_s=k[J_s] faithfully, since one a_i is nonzero. The kernels of evaluations at different a have different maximal radicals (Z_i-a_i), so CRT independently interpolates operator jets. The elementary syzygies generate a free B_s-module of rank n-1 at every nonzero a, and vanish at zero, giving s(n-1)(q^n-1) dimensions. The linear generator projections contribute n independent dimensions. For separating identities, (aJ_s)^q-aJ_s=a(N_s^q-N_s), which is nilpotent of exact index s whenever a != 0; hence the s-th power annihilates commutators in g_s but not in g_(s+1). All arbitrary-field and boundary quantifiers follow without relying on finite search. The packaged standard-library checker independently enumerates seven complete small-field term-function closures and eight identity tests, all passed.

value.rationale: The motivating literature explicitly studies growth of free algebras in locally finite Lie varieties and emphasizes the possibility that arbitrarily large modules have the same exponent q. Exact free-rank formulas for a natural indecomposable nonsemisimple family quantify what the exponent conceals: each additional Jordan layer changes every nontrivial rank by (n-1)(q^n-1). The associated simple explicit adjoint-polynomial identities distinguish all adjacent varieties, producing an infinite proper chain at fixed potential q. This is a structural family classification with a proof mechanism (operator-valued Hermite interpolation), not merely a checked small invariant or unsupported downstream claim.
